correctness.rationale: The primary published derivative identity reduces axis growth to the exactly specified signed geometric-block sum S_n. Signed endpoints are a finite geometric series. Scaling by T_j gives a continuous self-similar walk Φ with uniform convergence away from time zero; bounded normalized walks justify uniform Riemann convergence of the second Cesàro sum. An elementary convergent geometric integral gives D_gamma; differentiating its final-block profile identifies the sharp interior minimum -R_gamma. Both parity subsequences cover exactly the entire claimed cluster interval. An independent alternating geometric-block harmonic estimate proves logarithmic normalization Q_N→c with O(1/log N). Finite standalone exact integer and floating-point checks reproduce the identities and phase values but are not used as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The positive-measure wandering rectangle has known nonconvergent finite-time Lyapunov exponents. Whether standard arithmetic smoothing removes this instability is an intrinsic dynamical statistics question, not an arbitrary parameter selection. The theorem shows it fails, quantifies the strictly reduced yet nonzero interval via an interior logarithmic-phase extremum, and contrasts it with a convergent log-time weighting. This sharp two-weight boundary informs interpretation of finite-time Lyapunov estimates and is not supplied by the antecedent pointwise exponent interval alone.
